newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Kuchma slams Ukraine PM, deputies for late budget.
newsitem.headline: Kuchma slams Ukraine PM, deputies for late budget.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma lambasted his government and parliamentary deputies on Friday for failing to pass the much-delayed 1997 budget.

"We have seen a continuation of one of our worst traditions. The government has started the year without a budget and without several months' worth of revenues," he said in his annual speech in parliament, broadcast live to the former Soviet republic's 51 million people.
"We are in financial chaos," he added.
Government bore the biggest responsibility for the absence of a budget at the turn of the year and deputies had been too slow to work on it, he said.
Kuchma also accused Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko of proposing an "unrealistic" document in the first place.
The president said the only way to interpret the failure to pass the budget was as an attempt to force him to break the constitution by passing the budget by decree.
"Provoking me into taking unconstitutional action will not succeed," he said, to hoots from deputies who blame the government for not coming up with a revised document to debate.
Without a budget, which should have been passed on January 1 in line with the constitution, Ukraine cannot receive a $2.5 to $3 billion International Monetary Fund, long-term credit.
The budget and a package of tax reforms to underpin it are now unlikely to be passed before April, parliamentary speaker Olexander Moroz said recently.
